scope: 24 native missing-predictor axis obligations; not a finished valid-case denominator
julia_admission: No prepared joint missing-predictor engine or mi frontend found in targeted source audit; missing responses are a separate axis.

rows.claim_boundary: G2-adjacent evidence, weaker than its 12 sibling predictor-family cells below: tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-gaussian.R checks the TMB objective gradient at the optimum (max|grad| < 1e-2), the missing_data$predictors$x accounting/extractor contract (model_row, counts, random$enabled, structured$enabled), and the imputed() conditional-mode extractor (tolerance 1e-8) across three predictor-model variants: fixed-effect (version MD3a, lines 65-107), grouped random-intercept (MD3b, lines 109-150), and relmat()-structured (MD4, lines 152-257), each also combined with a response mask. Unlike the 12 sibling non-Gaussian predictor families, no hand-derived manual_*_mi_loglik() function cross-checks logLik(fit) against an independent formula for this family, so its likelihood-identity leg of the G2 gate rests on gradient-optimality rather than an explicit dnorm-based reference computation. It does not claim coefficient recovery against a known simulated true value, intervals, coverage, or bivariate responses (mi() inside a bivariate formula is explicitly rejected: tests/testthat/test-biv-student.R:456-460). REML is unavailable when a missing-data engine is active (R/drmTMB.R:277-290).

G2 evidence: a hand-derived manual_bernoulli_mi_loglik() reference (defined at tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-binary.R:26) computes the exact bernoulli mi() likelihood independently of the TMB objective and matches logLik(fit) to tolerance 1e-6 in "binary mi() predictor model uses exact two-state likelihood" (tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-binary.R:75), for a plain fixed-effect fit and again combined with response masking. Missing-predictor accounting (model_row, family, counts) and the imputed() extractor are also checked. This is a fixed-effect-only route: only the gaussian predictor family (cell mp-gaussian-gaussian) admits grouped or relmat()-structured predictor-model extensions; this family rejects (1 | group) predictor-model terms with 'fixed effects only'. It does not claim coefficient recovery against a known simulated true value, intervals, coverage, or bivariate responses. REML is unavailable when a missing-data engine is active (R/drmTMB.R:277-290).

G2 evidence only: manual_poisson_response_binary_mi_loglik() (tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-poisson-response.R:29) matches logLik(fit) to tolerance 1e-6 for the one-binary-missing-predictor route inside a poisson() response (test_that at line 66). Unlike its three sibling response-family cells below (binomial, nbinom2, beta), this route carries NO tolerance-based coefficient-recovery test against a known simulated true value: test-missing-predictor-poisson-response.R has no recovery test_that block (confirmed by inspection 2026-08-09; contrast with test-missing-predictor-{binomial,nbinom2,beta}-response.R, each of which has one). It does not claim coefficient recovery, intervals, coverage, or a non-binary missing predictor under this response family (a Poisson missing predictor under a poisson() response is explicitly rejected with 'binary missing predictor': test-missing-predictor-poisson-response.R:92-107). REML is unavailable when a missing-data engine is active (R/drmTMB.R:277-290).

G3 evidence: a single fixed deterministic DGP recovers the fitted response distributional parameters and the mi(x) predictor-model coefficients within tolerance 0.15 of their true simulated values in "binomial-response mi() recovers the response and predictor models" (tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-binomial-response.R:101): unname(coef(fit, "mu")), c(-0.2, 0.5, 1.0)) and unname(coef(fit, "mi_x")), c(0.3, 0.8) (both tolerance 0.15; lines 118, 120). This sits alongside a G2 manual_binomial_response_binary_mi_loglik() exact-likelihood cross-check (tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-binomial-response.R:34). This is a single deterministic-DGP point-fit recovery, not a replicated coverage study: no G4 interval or G5 repeated-seed coverage evidence exists for this route. It does not claim intervals, coverage, a non-binary missing predictor under this response family, or bivariate responses. REML is unavailable when a missing-data engine is active (R/drmTMB.R:277-290).

G3 point-fit recovery for two independent Gaussian mi() terms on a Gaussian response (drmTMB #963 option b). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-two-gaussian.R recovers response coefficients under MCAR (tolerance 0.20) and MAR/outcome-dependent missingness (tolerance 0.25), retains both predictors in missing_data$predictors, and requires imputed(fit, variable=) when k=2. This is not impute_joint (no residual correlation), not FIML across a SEM, not mixed predictor families, not k>2, and not a non-Gaussian response. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. Existing k=1 cell mp-gaussian-gaussian is unchanged.

G3 point-fit recovery for a Gamma(link=log) response with one binary mi() predictor (drmTMB #962 / S6 A7). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-gamma-response.R recovers mu c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7), log(CV)=log(0.3), and mi_x c(0.3, 0.8) under MCAR (tolerance 0.15, seed 13) and under outcome-dependent MAR (tolerance 0.20, seed 21). A G2 manual 2-point-sum logLik identity matches the TMB objective (tolerance 1e-6). This is not a continuous missing predictor, not k>=2, not impute_joint, not FIML across a SEM, and not lognormal/student/zi-*. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. Existing k=1 Gamma-as-predictor cell mp-gaussian-gamma is unchanged.

G3 point-fit recovery for an nbinom2() response with one Gaussian mi() predictor (drmTMB #962 / S6 A7 expand-gated cell). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-nbinom2-gaussian.R recovers mu c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7), log_sigma=-0.5*log(3), mi_x c(0.3, 0.8), and sigma_mi=0.40 under MCAR (tolerance 0.15, seed 27) and recovers mu / sigma / mi_x under outcome-dependent MAR (tolerance 0.20, seed 28). A G2 joint-density identity matches the TMB joint nll at the Laplace mode (tolerance 1e-6). This is not FIML, not impute_joint, not k>=2, not a grouped/structured predictor model, and not poisson/binomial/beta x gaussian. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. Existing mp-nbinom2-bernoulli is unchanged.

G3 point-fit recovery for a student() response with one binary mi() predictor (drmTMB #962 / S6 A7). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-student-response.R recovers mu c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7), log(sigma)=log(0.3), log(nu-2)=log(6), and mi_x c(0.3, 0.8) under MCAR (tolerance 0.15/0.15/0.30/0.15, seed 13) and under outcome-dependent MAR (tolerance 0.20/0.20/0.35/0.20, seed 21). A G2 manual 2-point-sum logLik identity matches the TMB objective (tolerance 1e-6). Density is drm_student_log_density; the shared 7-arg leaf ABI is unchanged. This is not a continuous missing predictor, not k>=2, not impute_joint, not FIML across a SEM, and not zi-*. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. Existing student missing-response cell is unchanged.

G3 point-fit recovery for a zi_poisson response with one binary mi() predictor in mu only and zi ~ 1 (drmTMB #962 / S6 A7 / D-23). tests/testthat/test-missing-predictor-zi-poisson-response.R recovers mu c(0.4, 0.5, 0.7), zi intercept logit(pi)=-0.8, and mi_x c(0.3, 0.8) under MCAR (tolerance 0.15, seed 13) and under outcome-dependent MAR (tolerance 0.20, seed 21). A G2 manual ZIP-mixture 2-point-sum logLik identity matches the TMB objective (tolerance 1e-6). A null DGP with beta_x=0 still recovers beta_x~0 so extra zeros do not load onto x. This is not a continuous missing predictor, not k>=2, not impute_joint, not FIML across a SEM, not mi() on zi, and not zi_nbinom2. No G4 interval or G5 replicated coverage. The 2-point sum inlines the ZIP mixture; it does not call the Poisson leaf.
